note: No [[identity.partition]]: the declared splits 1.5.answer-a and 1.5.answer-b name the native family's columns implicitly. CVID 20 delivers both columns as two literals of one source record. The blank-column CVID 22 and ANSWER_NEW (CVID 23), whose slug no split names, are support that no split takes (ANSWER_NEW is the replaced unique-suffix test's renamed sibling, with no pending split beside it). An independent [[errata.field]] renames CVID 20's ANSWER_A literal to ANSWER_B, the other split's column: the partition condition reads the original column, so the row stays answer-a and carries the corrected column. The replaced test's last leg (a new ANSWER_C member makes the converted partition stale) has no build form here: the build converts an implicit partition from the family it delivers, so a new member is converted with it; a pinned partition's drift is split-partition-native-stale-when-an-unreviewed-column-is-added.
fails_if: the partition's `when` column condition is evaluated against the [[errata.field]]-corrected column instead of the original, so CVID 20's ANSWER_A row moves to answer-b (or neither split takes it); or the condition is ignored, so both splits claim both literals of the shared CVID 20 record and its identity is withheld as conflicting; or `convert_column_partitions` assigns a literal whose slug no split names to a declared split, so ANSWER_NEW leaves the native family

sources.description: Variable 5 delivers, all in 2020, ANSWER_A and ANSWER_B as two literals of one record (CVID 20), a blank column (CVID 22) and ANSWER_NEW (CVID 23).
